questions.q: What triggers a Script Action to run?
options: A direct insert, update, or delete on a table, fired automatically by the platform
A named event firing, typically raised by code calling gs.eventQueue()
A user submitting a form on a client-facing page
Another Script Action completing successfully
questions.explain: A Script Action listens for a specific event name; it only runs when something's code explicitly raises that event via gs.eventQueue().

questions.q: What's the real distinction between a Business Rule and a Script Action, per this lesson?
options: A Business Rule is tightly coupled to a table's direct database operation; a Script Action is loosely coupled, reacting instead to an explicitly raised event
A Business Rule can only run client-side, while a Script Action only runs server-side
There's no real difference — they're two names for the same mechanism
A Script Action can only read data, never write it
questions.explain: A Business Rule fires automatically on a table operation; a Script Action fires only when someone's code chooses to raise the named event, keeping trigger and reaction decoupled.

options: The currently logged-in user's assigned vehicle
A hardcoded vehicle sys_id string
A query parameter from an incoming REST request
The vehicle reference field on the checkout GlideRecord passed in with the fired event
questions.explain: checkout holds the GlideRecord carried by the event (via event.parm1 or current), and .vehicle reads its vehicle reference field to look up the related vehicle record.

questions.q: What makes a Scheduled Script different from both a Business Rule and a Script Action?
options: It fires every time any table in the instance is updated
It runs on a time-based schedule with no triggering event or database operation at all
It requires a Scripted REST API to be defined first
It can only be written in a language other than JavaScript
questions.explain: A Scheduled Script is purely time-driven — it runs on its own schedule (e.g., nightly) regardless of anything a user or another script did.

options: It adds 90 days to every incident's closed_at field
It schedules the job to run again in 90 days
It deletes any incident closed more than 90 days ago
It sets cutoff to 90 days before the current date, so the query matches incidents closed earlier than that
questions.explain: addDaysUTC(-90) moves the GlideDateTime 90 days into the past, and the query then finds incidents closed before that cutoff.
